stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across El-Obeid, Kordofan to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.eraLabel: 1873 – 1881 · El-Obeid, Kordofan, Sudan
stops.imageCaption: Golden ochre acacia savanna stretching beneath a vast amber Sudanese twilight sky where a gentle white-bearded bishop shares water and grain beside a mud-brick schoolhouse.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Canonized in **2003**, **St. Daniel Comboni’s** prophetic last words came blazingly true: over **3,000 Comboni Missionaries**—priests, brothers, sisters, and lay volunteers from Africa, Latin America, Asia, and Europe—now serve the poorest communities in over **40 countries worldwide!**
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: St. Daniel Comboni famously called Africa ***"the poorest and most abandoned jewel of humanity"***—and insisted that true missionaries must *"make common cause"* with the people they serve in joyful solidarity!
stops.saintQuote: I am dying, but my work will not die—Africa will rise in light!

hiddenArtifacts.storyUnlocked: Deep inland in the savanna oasis of **El-Obeid**, Comboni founded joyful model villages of freed families—teaching carpentry, farming, literacy, and medicine! When catastrophic **drought, locusts, and famine** struck Sudan in **1878–1881**, friends urged the exhausted 50-year-old bishop to sail back to Italy to recover. Comboni refused to abandon his flock—giving away his last bread until he died peacefully in **Khartoum on October 10, 1881**, whispering: **"I am dying, but my work will NOT die!"**
